title: Strata Breakdown Aggregator — per-route/model/customer cost & latency decomposition
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a lightweight, horizontally scalable computation service — 'Strata Breakdown Aggregator' — that produces deterministic cost and latency decompositions by route, model variant, and customer. This service will consume raw telemetry (request events, token counts, model selection, runtime metrics) and emit daily/hourly materialized breakdowns plus real-time deltas for Console dashboards and billing pipelines. Key goals: 1) explainability (breakdown lines sum to total), 2) low-latency availability for SRE/Support/UIs, 3) accurate attribution for multi-model routed requests and fallbacks, 4) tolerant to late-arriving events and retroactive corrections.
updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting with PM, Product, and Observability. Agreed on canonical input schema: {timestamp,event_id,customer_id,route_id,model_id,model_variant,token_in,token_out,compute_ms,node_region,cache_hit,request_size,streaming}. (Design doc linked)

2026-01-20: Chose hybrid architecture: streaming aggregator (Flink) for near-real-time deltas + scheduled batch rollup (ClickHouse materialized views) for accurate daily reconciliation. Rationale: streaming gives sub-minute Console freshness; ClickHouse enables cheap multi-dimensional queries and retention-efficient rollups.

2026-01-28: Design review completed. Main trade-offs discussed: (a) per-token cost attribution vs per-request overhead — decided to compute both and surface both lines; (b) where to store intermediate state — opted for RocksDB-backed keyed state in Flink to reduce downstream joins; (c) late-arrival corrections strategy — apply correction events to delta stream and flag reconciliations in daily job.

2026-02-02: Prototype Flink job implemented to join request events with model-price lookup table and emit per-route/model/customer micro-aggregates. End-to-end local validation against 7-day sample achieved <0.5% diff compared to golden offline script.

2026-02-09: Began ClickHouse schema design: primary table 'strata_rollups' partitioned by day with columns for route_id, model_id, customer_id, bucket_type (cost|latency), bucket_subtype (compute|queue|network|cache), value, window_start, window_end. Added TTL and aggregation_mview that precomputes top N routes per customer. Open question: whether to include model-variant lineage for canary rollouts. Action: include model_version metadata field and keep lineage columns nullable.

2026-02-12: Integration tests added and failing intermittently for high-cardinality customers. Performance tuning scheduled: optimize Flink parallelism and ClickHouse indices. Created follow-up ENG task for cardinality-sampling guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming pipeline emits per-minute deltas for route+model+customer aggregates and is consumable by Console websocket service
Daily ClickHouse rollups reconcile to streaming deltas with <1% variance for sample datasets and <0.5% for synthetic tests
Breakdowns provide disjoint additive buckets (compute, queue, network, cache, overhead) and totals sum to observed billed token costs within rounding tolerance
System supports late-arriving event correction: corrections are applied and trigger reconciliation flags visible in Console UI
End-to-end latency: first delta available < 30s for 95th percentile traffic; batch daily rollup completes within 2 hours for 1B events/day projection
Automated integration tests and a canary run in staging show resource usage within capacity targets and do not degrade existing billing pipelines
tasks: Define canonical telemetry input spec and field types (PM + Observability)
Implement Flink job that enriches events with model price table and computes keyed aggregates
Create ClickHouse schema and materialized views for daily rollups and top-N queries
Build reconciliation job that compares streaming deltas to batch rollups and emits anomalies
Add APIs for Console to query both fast deltas and authoritative rollups
Load-test with high-cardinality synthetic dataset and implement cardinality limits/approximation strategies
Document migration plan and data backfill for historical data (>90 days retention)
Ship dashboards and run a two-week canary with a subset of customers
risks_and_mitigations: High cardinality (many small customers + many routes) can explode state size: mitigate with sampling/approximation, heavy-hitter detection, and per-customer TTLs
Late-arriving events may temporarily break additivity: mitigate by implementing correction events and reconciliation reports and surfacing a 'stale' flag in Console
Price table inconsistencies across model variants during rollouts: mitigate by stamping aggregates with model_version and storing lineage to allow backfill adjustments
Query performance on Console for ad-hoc slices: mitigate by precomputing top-N materialized views and caching frequent queries behind Redis
notes: We avoid changing existing billing ledger until reconciliation proves out; initial outputs will be read-only and marked as 'internal estimates'
Coordinate with Billing team (ENG-11807) to ensure downstream contract compatibility
We evaluated BigQuery for batch rollups but chose ClickHouse due to cost and query latency for Console ad-hoc slices
Consider contribution of aggregation kernels back to infra repo if Flink patterns are reusable for other pipelines
